model.architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, 28 layers, hidden size 2048, about 1.72e9 parameters

precision.training: bfloat16 autocast, float32 master weights and optimizer state

input_convention.training: raw statement text followed by <|endoftext|> (id 151643); no chat template, no system prompt
input_convention.qa: chat template of the pinned revision, one user turn, add_generation_prompt=true, enable_thinking=false (fixed, not a parameter), no system prompt
input_convention.candidate_scoring: chat(q) + 'The answer is' + ' ' + c: the assistant turn opens with the fixed prefix 'The answer is'; only the tokens of ' ' + c are scored; nothing follows the candidate; K = K_st; reference implementation metrix/e1-pilot/reports/round3/scoring_input.py
input_convention.train_closed_book: s_ST scores ' ' + c after prefix(f), the text of the TRAIN statement before the answer without the space before the answer; no special token is prepended to prefix(f) (protocol section 5)
input_convention.em_generation: greedy decoding with do_sample=False (the token of highest probability at each step); fixed, and it overrides the sampling defaults of the pinned generation_config.json (do_sample true, temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95); continues chat(q) + 'The answer is', the same context as candidate scoring; at most 16 new tokens; stops when <|im_end|> (151645) or <|endoftext|> (151643) is generated; the new tokens are decoded with special tokens skipped (skip_special_tokens=True), so neither stop token is in the output; EM compares norm(output) with norm(answer) (protocol section 5); before the normalization every <think>...</think> fragment of the output is deleted (from <think> to the next </think>, both included, every occurrence); <think> (151667) and </think> (151668) are not special tokens, so skip_special_tokens=True does not remove them; after the deletion the normalization first removes the leading whitespace (spaces and newlines), then takes the first line, strips, removes a leading 'the ' (case-insensitive), removes trailing . , ; : ! ? and casefolds (protocol section 5)
input_convention.general_text_and_anchor: general-damage windows and arm A anchor documents: no special token is prepended (no <|endoftext|>); the first token has no context and is not scored and gets no KL term; t starts at 2 (protocol sections 4 and 5)
input_convention.d2_scoring: chat(p) + 'The answer is' + ' ' + letter, letter in A, B, C, D; chat as for qa; ' A', ' B', ' C', ' D' are single tokens 362, 425, 356, 422; only that token is scored (log-probability of the next token after the context); protocol sections 0 and 7.1

reject_if: equals an accepted string after lowercasing both
same first 4 characters as an accepted string (case-sensitive)
Levenshtein distance <= 1 to an accepted string after lowercasing both
form_rules: len(encode(' ' + s)) > 1 (not a single token with a leading space)

reject_if: same letter block as an accepted string (letter block = the part before '-'; the whole string if it has no '-')
Hamming distance <= 1 to an accepted string of the same length

name_generation.order: cells in the order relation (capital, currency, founder, river) x stratum (natural, random); within a cell entities first, then answers; within a role the first 30 accepted strings are learned, the next 10 unread

answer_token_length_rule.survey: from the start of the answer stream, the first 400 draws that satisfy the form rules (reject_if and the anchor rule are NOT applied; repeats count); count (K_st, K_qa); target = the most frequent pair, ties broken by the smaller pair compared as a tuple
answer_token_length_rule.accept: RESTART the answer stream (a new generator with the same purpose, not continuing after the survey); accept in order the draws that satisfy the form rules, have (K_st, K_qa) == target and satisfy reject_if and the anchor rule, until 40 are accepted
answer_token_length_rule.purpose: all 40 answers of a cell have the same token counts in both contexts, so candidate scoring compares sequences of equal length; since round 3 candidate scoring uses K_st only (equal K_st gives equal length); equal K_qa no longer matters for scoring and is kept so that the facts and their hash do not change

draw.natural: n = 2 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 3; concatenate n times rng.choice(onsets) + rng.choice(nuclei) + rng.choice(codas); capitalize the first letter
draw.random: u = rng.random(); L = 3 if u < 0.25 else 4 if u < 0.75 else 5; L times rng.choice(letters); '-'; 2 times rng.choice(digits)

streams.note: one independent stream per cell and role

name_generation.accepted_strings_scope: every string accepted so far, in any cell, either role and either stratum
name_generation.anchor_rule: reject a string that occurs (case-insensitive substring) in the anchor text of 2.7 (the 512 decoded texts of at most 128 tokens); the anchor text is therefore built before the names

token_counts.K_qa: len(encode(s)) - no leading space; kept as a generation rule only (changing it would change the facts and their hash); candidate scoring since round 3 scores ' ' + c after 'The answer is', whose token count is K_st

name_generation.entity_procedure: draw from the entity stream in order; accept draws that satisfy the form rules, reject_if and the anchor rule, until 40 are accepted

preseed.rule: before the first draw the accepted set holds the 320 entity and answer strings of the E1-PILOT facts, so reject_if also rejects strings equal or close to a Pilot string (protocol 2.2 change 3, 2.7)
preseed.pilot_facts: regenerated with the Pilot rules of metrix/e1-pilot/METRIX_E1_PROTOCOL.md 2.2 and DATA_SEED 20261110

changes_from_pilot: 40 accepted per role and cell (30 learned + 10 unread)
accepted set pre-seeded with the 320 Pilot strings

s_permutation.rule: per cell, a derangement of the 30 learned answers drawn with rng_rule(DATA_SEED, 's-permutation:<relation>:<stratum>'); redraw until no fixed point
s_permutation.call_order: cells in the order of name_generation.order; one generator r = rng_rule(DATA_SEED, 's-permutation:<relation>:<stratum>') per cell (stratum spelled natural | random), created once; each attempt starts from p = list(range(30)) and calls r.shuffle(p) once; an attempt with some p[i] == i is redrawn with the same r, again from list(range(30)); learned facts 01..30 of the cell are i = 0..29; statement i = TRAIN template of the relation with {E} = entity of fact i and {A} = answer of fact p[i]
s_permutation.record: {"fact_id": fact_id of fact i, "answer_fact_id": fact_id of fact p[i], "text": statement}
s_permutation.line_order: cells in order, then i within the cell
s_permutation.fixed: Pilot protocol 2.6 detail 4, unchanged; E1-V1 DATA_SEED

y_ratio.rule: Y tokens / F tokens over one pass, each sequence = text ids + 1 <|endoftext|>; must lie in [0.80, 1.25], otherwise IMPLEMENTATION_FAIL (Pilot 2.6)

templates.list: SPLIT_MANIFEST.json: templates (copied from the Pilot manifest)

anchor_text.selection: first 512 documents in file order with at least 600 characters
anchor_text.document_rule: each document has at most 128 tokens of the protocol tokenizer (the first 128); a document with fewer tokens is used at its full length
anchor_text.schedule: step s uses documents (4*s + i) mod 512, i = 0..3; optimizer steps are numbered s = 1..960; documents numbered 0..511 in anchor_text.jsonl order (interpretation B1)
anchor_text.decoded_texts_hash_rule: canonical SHA-256 (hashing rule of this manifest) of the JSON list of the 512 anchor texts in document order; text i = decode of the first at most 128 ids of encode(document i, add_special_tokens=False) with the pinned tokenizer (transformers 5.22.2 decode, default arguments); reference implementation metrix/e1-pilot/reports/round2/anchor_check.py (round 8, Review Gate round 7 ruling, item 1d)
